chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We command our young children to fast when they are seven years old, with whatever they can endure of fasting the day. If it is until midday and more than that, or less, then when thirst and hunger overcome them, they break their fast, until they get accustomed to fasting and can endure it. So command your young children, when they are nine years old, with whatever they can endure of fasting. If thirst overcomes them, they break their fast.
ai.seo_question: At what age should children start fasting and how is it regulated according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the pedagogical method of *tadrij* (gradualism) in training children for obligatory fasting, distinguishing between the preparatory phase at age seven and the more rigorous practice at age nine. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on physical capacity and habituation over strict obligation, ensuring the child develops endurance without undue hardship before the age of *bulugh* (puberty).
